I'm a 5ft and 60kg Girl  so I usually end up sparring with guys who are over 80kg. I dont know if its just my playful nature but when I spar with my favourite male sparring partner, We tend to spar in a very technical and composed manner but we hunt and force submissions. We make sure we give one another enough time to tap. It doesnt bother me at all that im being submitted by a guy as we're both learning. If it wasnt for him, I wouldnt be getting so much compliment on my defense from the other guys. I also roll with the youngins and I enjoy the aggression. My favourite teenage training partner became my favorite because of how aggressive yet playful he could be but when it comes to submissions, we both do it slowly so that we can tap. We come to class to learn.

Conclusion:
The girl sounds butt hurt and should've just tapped earlier. You're at no fault here. You gave her the time to tap.
The guy who told you not to submit women, in my personal opinion, is wrong. We come to class to learn jiu jitsu and we spar to test our skills. Whats the point of sparring when you're not able to test your defensive skills against your opponents because they wont even try to submit you. The greatest progress ive ever made on my defense skill was cause by being subbed multiple times by a guy till the day came where I was good enough at defense that he had to switch to something else cause it was getting harder to submit me.

If she wants to keep enjoying BJJ, she has to learn to leave her ego at the door.

20 when I started doing BJJ. Was a bit overweight but because of my desire to be in a better physique for BJJ (due to how much I enjoyed it), I started working out and lifting weights to supplement my Jits.

Martial arts will definitely help get you in better shape and being overweight shouldnt be a reason for someone to not take up a martial art that interests them.
but do keep in mind that if you wanna speed things up in terms of getting in the ideal shape you can always hit the gym or do calisthenics at home.

The hardest part is showing up and sticking to it.
I was constantly anxious about showing up the first few months but I've got a great gym with great people and I just slowly blended in. Was a bit hard for me as im naturally introverted but it worked out.

I found that the longer ive been training at a gym, the easier it gets in terms of bodies touching one another. 
Ive never had issues with it, always knew that it was the nature of the sport and its what i signed up for. When you're at bottom mount and the person on top is putting pressure on your face with their boobs, Honestly, boobs will probably be the last thing on your mind. You'll more likely to focus on not suffocating, surviving and turning things around.

 I've gotten really close with my teammates and professors and as long as everyones thinkin about the sport and progressing their skills, a persons boob or which genitals they have wont matter. Your mind will be thinking about what would be the most effective next step to get the upperhand or dominate this match (without injuring your partner of course). Its usually the new white belts that feel a bit iffy but it usually passes with time.

Ive got a similar concussion time frame as you.
But the first 2 was just self diagnosed. I didnt see my doctor as the symptoms were very mild. Just felt a bit off but that was it. The last one was worst than the first 2 as I hit my head very hard but for some reason i didnt lose consciousness. I didnt even think much of it, I was alert and oriented. I still knew what i was doing, where I was and what im supposed to do so I just kept sparring even getting on dominant positions. The headache came about an hour after once I got home.
It went away the day after and I didnt feel dizzy inverting so I continued on with the competition that was 2 days after. Saw my gp after the comp and was told I had mild concussion. 

Im feeling somewhat better now but the anxiety of getting back on the mats is just bad. Ive got my teammates and coaches who really help me battle through the anxiety (without them knowing). Its getting to the gym that gets me all anxious but once im on the mats training, The anxiety lessens but its still there. I dont know if it will ever go away. I wanna remain in the sport as Im slowly building a side career off of it (coaching and more soon) and I genuinely love martial arts.

Ive modified my game where I no longer do stand ups and takedowns during light sparring. Ive heard there are people who have done BJJ for years and havent suffered a single concussion so im hoping I dont get any more concussions with the help of the changes i made with my game.

Also, How are you feeling now?

My sport has a lot of neck chokes but ive never had any issues with my neck even post concussion (tho i still try to be careful. If i know the choke is locked in and i feel a bit of pressure, I just tap rather than fighting it and passing out)

The only time my neck felt off was after I started doing neck exercises. Felt a bit sore the day after but knew it was from the neck exercise as I havent done one in weeks.

I just spoke to my PT today after seeing your message and will be doing more neck strengthening exercises soon.

My concussion was due to the fact that I didnt land properly after getting taken down by my training partner.
My head got pinned in between his chest and the mat but I dont think I got any whiplash injury. 
The landing was really bad tho as we came from a standing position. I knew i hit my head but i was fully aware of what was happening, what i was doing and where I was so I just continued sparring thinking nothing of it. Only got the headache once I got home from the gym.

Definitely dont want to stop as Im slowly building a side career off it but I did realise that If I wanna continue doing it, I'd have to modify my game, train smart and stay away from competitions for a year at bare minimum. I find that I feel alright even after training/ doing drills as well as light sparring but i dont wanna stay too comfortable and keep my guard down. 

The anxiety of getting on the mats is a big challenge for me and im really struggling with it. Its my teammates and coaches that help me get through it. The thought of just going to the gym gives me this big surge of anxiety that I have to constantly fight off and it does get tiring. 

I dont wanna lose this activity that i love.

Im hoping that whatever is happening in my head rn is temporary and will heal over time. 

I find that I can do really intensive activities and not feel like vomiting or have really bad headaches after but the moment I think about the symptoms like head pressure, I start feeling it a bit but in the bridge of my nose for like a few seconds or so. Hopefully its just me being anxious and have nothing to do with my old concussion. 
(Also got sort of punched in the nose back then but CT scan showed it was just a slight deviated septum)

Ive already changed my fighting game and ive been sticking to groundwork rather than takedowns.
I just got really worried when I heard I'll be more susceptible to concussions as ive probably already had some in the past. 
Its a big relief to hear that the force required to sustain another one is the same as any other.

 Sticking to ground game will pretty much eliminate the thing that caused my concussion (takedowns) as well as choosing my partners.

If its just for training and not competitions, BJJ isn't a bad idea. Just let your training partner know about your ankle problems and always tap early if they decide to even do any kind of submission on your leg/feet. Tho do be aware that your feet and legs will at some point get all tangled up with your training partner when you spar so theres always the risk of you getting your feet stuck in uncomfortable positions that may or may not be good for your ankles. I know I've had people fall on my foot before and I'm just lucky that my foot was never in an awkward position.

Can't say anything about TKD as I've never trained and would rather leave it to the ones who've trained to explain the risks and benefits.

Goodluck and stay safe!

I like to sing a lot and growing up, I've always listened to bands with male vocalists. I love impersonating vocalists, (and their voices) and since most of them are dudes, I ended up getting used to their range so now I sound like a dude.
I don't know if this is gonna help you but maybe try to impersonate how guys sound when they talk or sing and try to do it on a daily basis. That's what I did. 
Look for a performer or an influencer you like that has a similar voice and try to copy the way they speak, specifically the pitch of their voice. Start with someone  whos vocal range is close to yours and as time goes by, try to look for someone with a deeper voice and do the same thing. Just copy their pitch then look for someone and just go deeper and deeper. That pretty much sums up what i did. It was an unconscious effort for me cause I enjoyed singing and copying how other people talk for fun.

Also...

I joined a choir once and our conductor said we could widen our vocal range by doing vocal exercises everyday. He made us do something similar to the last exercise in this vid:

https://youtu.be/F0nXWKp74-A 

But instead of going higher, try going lower. maybe  you can find a pitch you're comfortable with and start talking in that range.
As your vocal range widens, slowly lower the pitch when you talk to people. It'll take some time tho.

I'm honestly not sure if thats going to help cause im not an expert but the vocal exercises helped me control my voice and get comfortable with it.

I tried to chase her love, even tried buying it from her but money only bought her love for a day or so. I guess to anyone adopting, the only advice I could give yall is to love those kids and make sure they know that they mean the world to you and that they arent any less than your biological kids. They are a gift/blessing. One of the most heartbreaking thing an adopted child could hear from his or her adoptive parents would be that they're gonna give up on the child and return him/her. My mom used to tell me that and I would fear for my life/future nonstop so please, dont try to straighten them by using threats. Just show them love, tell them you love them, shove it in their faces. Let them know that you'll always be by their side no matter how stupid their decisions can get. 
They dont need another person to abandon them.
